facts.text: The Choctaw Railroad reached Ola in 1899 after Harkey granted access on the condition that the railroad be named for the town and guarantee stops for 99 years.
Nimrod Lake and Dam on the Fourche La Fave River lie about 9 miles southwest of Ola, forming a reservoir that shapes regional water flow and offers waterfront.
Ola’s climate supports a 200‑220 day growing season, making it ideal for crops like soybeans and rice.
After the war, Ola attracted immigrants from Georgia, North Carolina, and Tennessee, drawn by inexpensive land and new economic opportunities.
Ola began as Red Lick, was renamed Petit Jean in 1866, and finally adopted the name Ola when the post office changed in 1880.
The first house in Ola was completed in 1860 by homesteader Elisha Harrel.
